answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identities share fate: each newcomer posts a bond into a small mutual pool with the peers who vouch for it, and the pool pays out only while every member keeps a steady pulse of honest, distinct work. If one member is caught cheating, the whole pool is slashed at once, so a fable of cheap fake accounts collapses: each extra identity adds its own bond to the shared risk, and one detection burns the whole ring, an ember that spreads to every sockpuppet at once.
